extra.reason: Implemented as a new 'Hotkeys' row in the in-game menu (src/game_menu.c/.h, src/main.c hotkeys_screen()) plus diatom-side dispatch (separate repo commit, feature/1v7.2-hotkey-submenu there: src/hotkeys.c/.h, hotkey_chord() in main.c, HOTKEYS/SETHOTKEYS protocol verbs, diatom ADR-0035). Resolved both open architectural questions the bead itself flagged: (1) STORAGE SHAPE -- mirrors turbo.<tag>'s existing sqlite precedent exactly (src/platform.c plat_hotkey_map/plat_hotkey_set), one compact binding string per system tag, no shipped default since this is new/opt-in. (2) DISPATCH LOCATION -- lives in Diatom, not the launcher: confirmed by reading diatom's own frame loop that gameplay input is polled by Diatom while the launcher is blocked on the protocol socket for the whole session, so a hotkey that must fire during live play (not only while the launcher's paused menu has focus) has to be detected there. (3) BUTTON BUDGET -- turbo.md's per-system spare-button concern does not apply at all: hotkeys require SELECT held (extending diatom's existing display_chord convention), which is never held during normal gameplay or by turbo's own plain-button remapping, so no collision is possible by construction, on any system. UI is 4 fixed rows (Fast-Forward, Rewind, Quick Save, Quick Load) cycled left/right through a short candidate list (None, L2, R2, X, Y) -- deliberately NOT a 'press any button to capture it' flow, which this codebase has never built anywhere and would have been the highest-risk new interaction to write with zero ability to run it; the left/right-cycle shape reuses Display Mode's own already-proven interaction instead. VERIFICATION: TortOS side -- new tools/hkbind-check.c (wired into make check as check-hkbind) drives the real parser/serializer with no SDL: round-trip, empty-clears, malformed-input-ignored-not-crashed, buffer-truncation-safety, all pass; tools/menu-check.c extended for the new row and still passes; check-db regression-checked. Diatom side -- full non-port tree compiles clean; new SDL-free harness drives hotkeys.c's real parser (21 assertions: accept path, every refusal shape); proto-speed-check.c extended for the new wire verbs; check-seam/check-register/check-corefacts/check-rates all pass (register's own line-length check caught and I fixed a too-long entry). NOT verified anywhere: the actual per-frame chord dispatch and the screen's rendering/input handling, both of which need SDL to compile in an environment that has none and no privilege to install it -- reviewed by hand, including catching a real bug this way (a stale forward declaration with the wrong parameter count).
